answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the saffron check immediately, the meadow audit keeps the resolved set and the summit replay makes public exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 254 aliases thus burns the reading cost 254 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 37 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
